note: Entry into the DT_HASH lookup path; hashtab points to the attacker-controlled DT_HASH table in the ELF file image.
n_bucket is read directly from the untrusted DT_HASH header; a large value expands the bucket array size used for subsequent indexing.
buckets points just past the two header words of DT_HASH; its extent is derived from n_bucket.
chains is computed as buckets + n_bucket; the actual allocated table may be shorter than this pointer arithmetic implies.
l_hash is set to the end of the DT_HASH region from the dynamic section offsets; used only for a weak sanity check.
The bucket index m is derived from the lookup name and n_bucket; with a crafted n_bucket this selects an arbitrary bucket slot.
Only checks that the bucket slot is before l_hash; does not validate the chain index si read from that slot.
si is taken from the bucket slot and used as an index into chains without any upper-bound check against the actual table size.
When si is large (attacker-controlled), &chains[si] points past the end of the DT_HASH allocation; get_te32 performs a 4-byte heap out-of-bounds read.
The OOB read at chains[si] occurs before this check, so the malformed chain index triggers the heap-buffer-overflow read first.
